Final_Translation: Salutation to Sri Ganesha. Janamejaya spoke: "O Bharata, O grandfather, as this autumn-like season has arrived, how did the great soul cast off his mortal body, and what yoga did he hold onto?" Vaishampayana spoke: "Listen to this, O king, with a pure mind and concentrated intellect, as I describe how the tiger among the Kurus, Bhishma, resorted to the casting off of his body. At the setting of the sun, when the sun had moved to the north, he absorbed his soul into the Supreme Self, with a focused mind, on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Magha."

Final_Translation: May Vishnu, who abides in the supreme half and takes unto Himself the deities residing within the bones and joints, be pleased with the well-wishers.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: ब्रह्मस्पतेष्ट्वा साम्ना ज्येना त्रिषंचं म्यसावितिमा- मथ कृतित दृहस्पते रेवेनमेत सायुज्यं सतोकृतांगमयति २४। अथा ह सम्राड्युम स्सोसम्राड्युमसा वितिनिवदितमेवेनमेत संतांद्वेण्यो निोदययेयंहमावीर्योयोप्य ५२. बेचीयेयंखुष्पाणो कोर्त्तनगोपायतेत्येवेन ५१. दाह त्रिष्ट्चा आहत्वि रदियङ्गः १२५। अथो जितीः जुहोति वा वाचयतिवायदि जुहोति यदिवाच यति समानमेवबंधुः ११६ सद्याचयति अग्नि रेकाक्षरेण प्राणमुदययन्मुजे षं प्रजापतिः सप्तदशाक्षरेण सप्तदशा५ स्ताम मुदययत् मुज्जेषमिति तद्युदेवताभिरेतादेवताउदज्
Final_Translation: By the Sāman of Brahmanaspati, with "By the triad, may you be protected,"—thus he unites him with Brahmanaspati himself, bringing him into direct communion. Then, "O Emperor, with splendor, O Emperor, with splendor,"—thus he makes him prosperous. "May the vital breath, the eye, the ear, the speech protect him,"—thus he protects him with these. He speaks with a triad to the hotṛ priest. Then he offers the oblations of victory, or has them recited; whether he offers them or has them recited, the connection is the same. He causes them to be recited. Agni, with a single syllable, raising up the prāṇa, conquered; Prajāpati, with the seventeen-syllabled [Stoma], conquered the seventeenfold Stoma. Indeed, whatever deities [conquered] with these deities, they conquered.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: श्रीः कृ०आ० हृ० ७५२ ब्रह्ममित्रस्यवरुणस्यशर्म्मपस्यामुरुवीराअरिष्ठाः ॥ तिस्रोभू मीर्धारेयत्रीरुतथ्यूँत्रीणिब्रताविध्येअंतरेषां। ऋतेनादित्यामहि वोमहिलंतदर्यमन्वరుణमित्रचाह ॥ त्रीरोचनादिव्याधारयंत हिरण्ययाःशुचयोधार्तपूतः । असञ्जतोअनिमिषा अदब्धा उरुशंसारञ्जवेमर्त्याय ॥ त्वंविश्वेषाम्वरुणसिराजायेदेवा असुरयेवमर्त्ताः । शनन्नैराजस्वफारदोविचेशेषणमायुँषिषधि तानिप्पूर्वा ॥ ४ ॥ नदक्षिएणविचिकेतेनसध्यामप्राचीनमादि त्पानोतपप्या । पाक्काविद्वसोधधीयाविचधुष्यानीतोअभयं ज्योतिरेषां ॥ योराजञ्बपकृतंनिम्भोदद्दाथ्यंवर्धयंतियुष्ठ यञ्चनित्याः । सरेवान्यातिप्रथमोश्खेनवसुधोवाविधेय सुँप्रशस्तः ॥ शुचिरपःसुयवसाभदधउपक्षेतिऋड्वयाः सु वीरः । नकिष्टंस्त्रंपतितोनदूरघवआदित्यानांभवतिप्रणीतौ ॥
Final_Translation: May we attain the wide, hero-filled, and unharmed shelter of Mitra and Varuna. Three are the earths, supporting the threefold waters; three are the ordinances maintained among them. By truth, O Adityas, great is your mighty power; Aryaman, Mitra, and Varuna, this I acknowledge.  The golden, pure, and sanctified ones hold the three heavenly realms of light. Unsleeping, unblinking, and undeceived, they are of wide praise, swift, and protecting for mortals.  O Varuna, you are the king of all, of gods as well as mortals, belonging to the Asura realm. Grant us safety, O King; prolong our lives for the days that lie ahead.  Who perceives the south, who perceives the east, the north, and the west, so that no heat may burn us? Wise and firm in intellect, they establish protection and light for them.  O King, who removes the evil done and makes the truth grow, and who is ever watchful, the wealthy one moves forth first with a swift horse, worthy of praise and to be revered with oblations.  Pure, with waters, rich in good pasture, and firm in his abode, he dwells upright and blessed with heroes. None overcomes them, nor do they fall far away, who are in the guidance of the Adityas.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: मउम्म्रायचावस्वऱ्यायचनमोनोदेयायचनदीप्पायच ३१ नमो ज्येष्ठायचकनिष्ठाय चनमः पूर्वजायचापरजायचनमोमध्यमायचापगल्भायचनमो जघन्यायचबुध्धायच नमः सोब्याय ॥३२॥ नमः सोब्यायचप्रतिशर्यायचनमोयाम्यायचक्षेम्यायचनमः श्लोक्या यच्छावसान्यायचनमउर्ध्र्यायचषब्द्यायचनमोवन्याय ॥३३॥ नमोवन्यायचक्षत्ता यचनमः अवयायचप्रतिश्रवायचनमः आशुषेणायचाशुरथायचनमः शूरयायचानोदिने चनमोविस्मिन ॥ ३४ ॥ नमोविल्मिनेचकवाविनेचनमोवर्णिणेचवरूथिनेचनमः श्रुता यचश्रुतसेनायचनमोऽहुप्यायचाहनन्यायचनमो ध्र्सवे ॥ ३५ ॥ नमोध्र्सवेचप्रम शायचनमोनुषङ्गिणेचिषुधिमतेचनमस्तीक्ष्णेषवेचायुधिनेचनमः स्वायुधायचसुध न्वनेच ॥ ३६ ॥ नमः सुत्याय ॥ नमः सुत्यायचपस्यायचनमः काद्यायचनीप्पायचनमः

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: सं० : ९ श्री हुँटिराजादिषट्पंचाशत्नमपतियों नमः ॥ ॐ ॥ अग्निमीळे पुरोहितं यज्ञस्य देवमृत्विजम् । होतारं रत्नधातमम्॥ अग्निः पूर्वेभिर्षिभिरिडू नूनैरुतौ स देवौ इह वक्षति॥ अग्निना रयिमश्नवत्पोषमेव दिने दिने। यशसं वीररंवतः ॥ अग्नेययज्ञमध्वरंविश्वतः परिभूरसि ॥ स इदेवेषुगछति। अग्निहोतोकविक्रतुः सत्यश्चित्रश्रवस्तमः । दिवोदेवेभिरागमतू ॥ यदंगराशुषेत्वमग्नेभदंकरिष्यसि । तवेत्तत्सल्यंसंगिरः॥ उपत्वांग्नेदिनेदिनेदोषावस्तर्धियावयम् ॥ नमोभरंतमसिराजंतमध्वराणांगोपामृतस्यदीदिविं वर्धमानस्वेदमोसनः पितेवसुनवेग्नेसूरूपाउन्नोस्वासुवस्वानःस्वस्तये॥१॥ वायोवायाच्रिदेशेतमेसोमाअरंकृतः तिबापा हिश्रुधीहर्वावाय
Final_Translation: Salutations to the fifty-six revered lords, beginning with Sri Huntiraja. Om. I praise Agni, the domestic priest of the sacrifice, the divine minister, the invoker, the best bearer of treasures. May this Agni, praised by ancient sages and modern ones as well, bring the gods here. Through Agni, one attains wealth, increasing day by day, glorious and rich in heroes. O Agni, you encompass the sacrifice and the ritual on all sides; you truly go among the gods. Agni is the offerer, wise in will, true, most glorious in renown; may he come with the gods from heaven. O Agni, whatever auspicious deed you will do for the pious worshipper, that truth belongs to you alone, O Angiras. Approaching you, O Agni, day by day, at evening and at dawn, we bring our homage to you—the ruler of the dark, the protector of sacrifices, the shining guardian of the cosmic order, growing in his own abode. Therefore, O Agni, be easy of access to us like a father to his son. Abide with us for our well-being. O Vayu, O Vayu, the Soma juices have been prepared for your three regions; do thou drink, hear our call, O Vayu.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: श्रीः शं १ ॥श्रीगणेशायनमः ॥श्रीपुरुषोत्तमाय नमः ॥श्रीकीर्तनादः वनंप्रयेतियस्यसंसारत्तागटाः उमादिभिष्तंशेषंभेजरामसुरुरू स्तमः ॥ रागादिरेगान्स्तानाव्यक्तानशेषकायप्रस्तानानेशक्ष न ॥ सैत्सकामोटारतिदान्त्यानयोसर्ववैद्यायनमोस्तंतसे ॥ ग्रथान्ननाग्राक्षमीयसध्यायेव्याख्यास्यामः इत्यनःसाङ्गमेया ग्रामतर्षयः आयुषकामायमानेनथमाथैसवसाधनम् आयुर्वे दोरपदेशेउविधेयःपरमादरः ब्रह्मासरत्तायुषोवेद्रेप्रजापतिः मत्रिजदान्नोाश्विनौतोमस्त्रस्वातंमौणिउटासिकास्थनीन् ने गिनवेर्शादिकास्तेतएथऋक्षेवाणिनिनिरे तभेषातिविषकीणींभः प्रायःसारनरोस्मयः क्रियतेशंगरुदयेनानिसेतिप्रविस्तृतम् कायबालग्रहदोंगशल्यदंशजगजस्थान ग्रछ्यावेगानितस्याइ चिकित्सानोपमेस्थिता वायुःपित्रकफभेतिशयोदोषाःसमासतः॥ रामः
Final_Translation: May auspiciousness prevail. Salutations to Lord Ganesha. Salutations to the Supreme Purushottama. Salutations to the resplendent source of glory.   He whose worldly bonds are severed, whom Uma and others worship, who is the serpent Sesha, the lord of gods, and the dispeller of darkness—salutations to Him, who is the healer of diseases rooted in attachment, who manifests the unmanifest, who is the refuge of the devoted, and who is the ultimate physician of all.   Now, we shall expound the chapter known as [the compilation], as declared by the sages. For one desiring a long life, righteousness, wealth, and the means to attain them, utmost regard should be paid to the teachings of Ayurveda. Brahma remembered the Veda of longevity and imparted it to Prajapati. Prajapati taught it to the Ashvins, and they to Indra. Indra transmitted it to Atreya and other sages. They, in turn, composed various treatises for the benefit of all beings.   Thus, this comprehensive science [Ayurveda] is established, dealing with the eight branches: internal medicine, pediatrics, psychiatry [or diseases of the head and neck], major surgery, toxicology, rejuvenation, and virilizing therapies.   In brief, the bodily humors (doshas) are three: Vata (wind), Pitta (bile), and Kapha (phlegm).

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: विकृताविकृतादेहैर्येज्ञ्ज्ञनिनेवर्त्तयेतिचे । तेषामिपेपिश्राम्यो रफोपमेोधेसंघ्रयः । वयोसेशरात्रिभुक्तानांतेतम्मध्येदिगाः क्रु । मात् तैर्भेवेहिषम्क्तीतामन्दामिः समैः समः । कोष्ठः क्रूरोम ुर्म्मेषामप्वास्थालैः समैरपि । मुक्ततवस्थैर्जन्मादौविषेणोषवि षक्रिमैः । तैसंसिसः प्रकृतयोक्षीनमध्येप्रमः । एथक् समधात समस्तास्तुप्रेशूनियादितोधत्ता तत्रर्त्तोताक्षुः शीतः नरः सप्त म्लोलनिलेः । पित्रेमस्सेरतीतोमसेनतुविखैसमंरश्वम् स्त्रियः । शोणितगरूमेदः स्थतोमृरक्ततः स्थिरः कफः । मेसर्म्सोमिश्रातश्च तद्धिर्वितयकोपतः । रसास्लेमां समेदोस्थिमज्जाशुक्राणिधातवः सप्रहव्यामलामुत्रशक्रत्सेदाटयोधरत् । वृढिः समैः सर्वेषां विपरेतैविपर्ययः । रसाः स्वादुप्रलवणतिक्तोष्णकषायकाः । षड्द्रव्यमाश्रितास्तेसक्तयथाएवैबन्नायदाः । तत्रयामार्ततंज्ञेनि
Final_Translation: If it is asked whether one should not treat those whose bodies are altered or unaltered by poisons, [we reply:] for them, the application of therapies [should be undertaken] like [treating] the exhausted or the afflicted. For those whose day and night are spent in consuming [improper food], they become enraged in the middle [of the body] due to the accumulation of the humors. Thus, they become afflicted by poisons, counter-poisons, and insects, along with their digestive fire being impaired, yet remaining balanced. Their bowel movements are cruel, soft, or hard, and likewise [affected] by unwholesome elements. Being situated in their natural states at birth, they become afflicted by poisons, counter-poisons, and insects. Through these [factors], their constitutions become disturbed, with depletion and obstruction in the middle [part of the body]. Having understood this separately, combined, or in a balanced state of the humors, one should administer treatments accordingly. There, the man becomes afflicted by the cold season, [or] by the derangement of wind. With bile and phlegm surpassed, and after a month, it is equal to... Women [are characterized by] blood, muscle, fat, bone, marrow, and semen, where phlegm is stable due to being situated in blood. Mixed with fat and marrow, this is caused by the aggravation of the two [bile and wind]. The seven bodily tissues are rasa (nutritive fluid), rakta (blood), mamsa (muscle), medas (fat), asthi (bone), majja (marrow), and shukra (semen), along with waste products such as feces, urine, and sweat. The increase of all these [occurs] by things similar [in qualities], and their decrease by the opposite. Sanskrit_OCR_Text: राम० १ ॥श्रीगणेशायनमः अथद्वितीयः पादः उद्दिष्टः समाहितचित्तस्य योगः कथंमुत्थितचित्तोपियोगयुक्तः स्यादित्येतदुत्तरमारभ्यते तपस्वा ध्यायेश्वरप्रणिधाना निक्रियायोगः १ नार्तापसविनोयोगसिध्यति अनादिधारककर्मवासनां चित्राप्रकृष्ठकष्टापितविषयजाला चांसुद्धि र्नान्तरेणतपः संभेदमापद्यते रुतितपसमुपादानेन च चितप्रसा दनमबाधमानमनेनासेव्य मितिमन्यतेस्वाध्यायः प्रणवादिप वित्रमंत्राणांजपः मोक्षशास्त्र्रध्यायनंवा ईश्वरप्रणिधानेसर्व क्रियाणांपरमगुरौवर्णं तत्फलसंन्यासोवा सहिक्रियायोगः समाधिभावनाअर्थः क्लेशतनूकरणार्थश्च २ सहिज्ञासेव्यमा शिक १
Final_Translation: Salutation to Lord Ganesha. Now the second pada is introduced.   How can a person whose mind is restless become united with yoga, just like one whose mind is collected? To answer this question, the text begins:   Austerity (tapas), study of sacred texts (svadhyaya), and devotion/surrender to the Lord (ishvara-pranidhana) constitute Kriya Yoga. Otherwise, yoga does not succeed for one whose mind is afflicted.   Without the piercing refinement of austerity, the impurity of the mind—which is characterized by beginningless subconscious karmic impressions, multifaceted, and deeply afflicted by the entanglements of sense objects—cannot be dissolved.   Through the practice of austerity, the pacification of the mind is achieved without hindrance; hence, it is considered worthy of being practiced.   "Study" (svadhyaya) means the repetition (japa) of sacred mantras such as Om, or the study of scriptures on liberation.   "Devotion to the Lord" (ishvara-pranidhana) means the dedication of all actions to the supreme guru, or the renunciation of the fruits of those actions.   Verily, this is Kriya Yoga, which serves the purpose of fostering meditative absorption (samadhi) and bringing about the attenuation of mental afflictions (klechas), and it ought to be practiced.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: यदादमथशब्दोविकारार्थमदैपथावयर्थसंपचनइत्याह योमानुशासनशास्त्रमधिकृतमिति ननुवाख्यायमानन्यायोगोवाधिकारुणतो मनुशास्त्रमित्यंत आह वेदितव्यमिति मृत्यं श्रुत्वाख्यायमानन्यायोग इत्युनमतुतनदि मयेराशास्तेणकारोनयुतायै करसा गोचरस्य युता दकस्यव्यापारोनकर्मगोचर इतिकर्तृव्यापारविवक्षयायोगविषयत्यशास्त्रस्याधिकारुतात्त्वंदितव्यं शास्त्रव्यापारगोचरतया नुयोगएवा धिकृततिभाव अधिकारार्थस्यचाथवा द्स्याग्यार्थेनीय मानोनकुनदकीननिबप्रब्रोर्मगलालदिनल्यत्६ जिमेनवे शब्दसंदेतनि क्तिमर्थ संदेहतुनपन्यति योगःसमाधि युमसमाधावितस्यहा घुल्यन्त्र समाधपर्थे नतु युजिर्मोगे र्यस्मातंसयो गार्थइत्यर्थै । ननु योगा अनुशासनेशास्त्रमधिकृतं वेदितव्यम्। योगःसमाधिः । नचसमाध्र्यमोगः। चित्तस्यधर्मः॥
Final_Translation: When the word "atha" [now] is used in the sense of an auspicious beginning, some state that it serves the purpose of an introductory prerequisite. Regarding the statement, "Now, the treatise on Yoga is to be expounded," one might object: Is not Yoga [mental absorption] the subject matter, rather than the treatise of Manu? Anticipating this, the text says, "is to be understood." Having heard this death, the notion that the exposition is a process of connection is refuted; just as the activity of water does not pertain to action, but rather—intending to express the agency of the doer—the treatise has the sphere of its authority in the subject of connection, because it falls within the scope of the treatise's operation, the very process of inquiry is indeed authorized, such is the underlying intent.   Moreover, the word "atha," denoting an auspicious beginning, when interpreted in the sense of an auspicious start, is not [intended] for [mere] word-play or the embellishment of a composition. Nor does the inquiry raise a doubt regarding the meaning of the terms; rather, "Yoga" means *samadhi* [deep meditative absorption], derived from the root *yuj* in the sense of *samadhi*. Therefore, [Yoga here] has the meaning of *samadhi*, and not *yuj* in the sense of mere union [connection], because its meaning is that of *samadhi*.   Thus it is established: "Now, the treatise on Yoga is to be understood. Yoga is *samadhi*. And *samadhi* is not [mere] union; it is a property of the mind."

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: न तणादिर्वाच्यश्वावकालो भेषजयोगकृत् शोधनेशाम ने चेति समासयो षधंदिधा शरीरज्ञा नारोधा एणक्रमेण परमौ षधम्। ततत्रिरेको वमनेन तथा तैलाभ्यञ्जनमधुः पीवैर्यान्ताशि विक्तामनोरोधोषधेपःम् भिषट्रयाएप् पस्यातारोवीपादा चतश्चयं चिकिन्सितस्थानि रिष्टं प्रते केचश्रश्रुगुणांस दत्त्लो यात्रशास्वा योतस्कमासुविभिषक् वञ्चकल्याउहूर्यणेमः सञ्रयोगपमोधथम् अत्ररक्तसुविदेत्तो मतिमान्मार्गवारके आग्निरेगीभिषग्वेशे पात्ताप कस्सात्वानापे सर्वौषधत्तमेः रेदेरुनः पुंसोजितात्मनः श्रमन्मगोल्यदेतत्रइपइपोनुपद् वः मृतलघ्हरोगेनप्रतिपार सेपरि गृहेषनुगलोयेकदो धमागोडासृवतः शस्त्रादिसाधनः क्रुद्धसंवरेवतनागदः शेषहता रायेवायाळः पञ्च्याम्पासाहिपयंगे अत्रणक्रसपवः
Final_Translation: Not grass and the like are to be spoken of, nor is *avakāla* (a kind of aquatic plant) the creator of medicinal combinations for purification. Nor are these two compounds thus; rather, medicine is twofold according to the knowledge of the body and the prevention of ailments, and in this due order, it is the supreme medicine. Then, triple [treatment] through emesis, as well as oil-anointing, drinking of honey, and [therapies] for pacifying the afflicted mind—these are the prescriptions of the physician. Those who understand this are the dispellers of troubles. Fourfold is the place of treatment, and certain ones, having given the qualities of the hearer, [perceive them]. Therefore, let the physician, skilled in the sequence of procedures, apply the combination for the welfare and delight [of the patient]. Here, the intelligent [physician], knowing well the vitiated blood that obstructs the channels, like fire [consuming fuel], and entering the body of the physician [as well], becomes the best of all physicians, protecting [the patient] from suffering. For a self-controlled man, free from fatigue, there is no misfortune arising from disease. Protected in the home by a gentle disease-free state, [he attains] the ultimate dharma. Free from the flow of blood and weapons and the like, enraged yet restrained, he is free from venom. The slain are protected, or [they are] like serpents in the fivefold breath. Here are the [proper] paths regarding these.

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: ताभ्यां वा मनसः स्थितिं संपादयेत्॥३५॥ विषयवती वा प्रवृत्तिरुत्पन्ना मन सः स्थितिं निबंधनी॥ नासिकाग्रे धारयतो अस्यादिव्यगन्धसंवित्सगंधप्रव ृत्तिः॥ जिह्वाग्रे दिव्यरससंवित् तालुनि रूपसंवित् जिह्वामध्ये दिव्यस्पर्शसं वित्॥ जिह्वामूले दिव्यशब्दसंवित् इत्येताः प्रवृत्तयउत्पन्नाश्चित्तस्थितौ निबध्नीति संशयं विधमंति· समाधिप्रज्ञायाश्च द्वारी भवंतीति· एतेन च द्रादियग्रह मणिप्रदीपपरस्मादिषु प्रवृत्तिरुत्पन्ना विषयवत्येव वेदितव्या॥ यद्यपि तत्र शास्त्रानुमानाचार्योपदेशैः अवगतमर्थन तं प्रज्ञोतमेव भवति एतेषांयथाभूतार्थप्रतिपादनसामर्थ्य तथापि यावदेकदेशोपि कश्चिन्द्रि यकरणा संवेद्यो भवति तावत्सवै परोक्षमिव अपवर्गादिषु सूक्ष्मेष्वर्थेषु न दृढां बुद्धिमुपादयति। तस्माच्छास्त्रानुमानाचार्यैपदेशयोर्दलनाथ्
Final_Translation: Or through those [practices], one should attain the stability of the mind. Alternatively, a sense-perceiving mental activity, when it arises, serves to bind the mind to stability. For one who concentrates on the tip of the nose, there arises the experience of divine fragrance, which is a fragrance-perceiving activity. At the tip of the tongue is the experience of divine taste; on the palate, the experience of form; in the middle of the tongue, the experience of divine touch; and at the root of the tongue, the experience of divine sound. These very activities, when they arise, bind [the mind] to the state of consciousness, dispel doubts, and become the gateways to the wisdom of *samādhi*. By this same principle, it should be understood that when an activity arises regarding things such as space, stars, gemstones, lamps, or the supreme, it is likewise sensorially oriented (*viṣayavatī*). Although the true meaning has been understood through scriptures, inference, and the instructions of a preceptor, it does not become the highest wisdom possessing the capacity to manifest things exactly as they are. Nevertheless, as long as even a single aspect becomes directly knowable through the sensory faculties, everything else remains, as it were, unperceived, and fails to produce a firm conviction regarding subtle matters such as liberation and the like. Therefore, for the sake of shattering [doubts] through the scriptures, inference, and the preceptor's instruction—

Sanskrit_OCR_Text: पातं. १३ मेवावश्यं कश्चिदर्थविशेषः प्रक्ष्षीकर्त्तव्यः। तत्र तदुपदिष्टार्थेकदेश- प्रक्षेते सति सर्व्वसुसूक्ष्मविषय्मपि आपवर्गांतं गृह्यते। एतदर्थमेवे- दंचित्तपरिकर्म्म निर्दिष्ट्यते। अनियतासु वृत्तिषु तद्विषयायां वशीकारसं- ज्ञायामुपजातायां समर्थस्यात् तस्य तस्यार्थस्यप्रक्षीकरणाय तथा च स- तिश्रद्धावीर्य्यस्मृतिसमाधयोऽस्याप्रतिबंधेन भविष्यंतीति॥ ३५॥ विशोका- वाज्योतिष्मती पुरुषस्य॥ प्रवृत्तिरुत्पन्ना मनसः स्थितिं निबंधनीमनुव र्त्ततेहृदयपुंडरीकेधारयतोयाबुद्धिसंवितुः॥ बुद्धिसंविद्धि भास्वरमाकाशक- ल्प्यं॥ तत्र स्थितिर्वैशारद्यात्तः प्रकृतिः सूर्येदुग्रहमणिप्रभारूपाकारेण वि कल्यते। तथा चास्मितायां समापन्ने चित्ते निस्तरंगमहोदधिकल्प्यं शांतुमु नंतमस्मितामात्रं भवति। यत्रेदमूक्तं तमणुमात्रमात्मानमनुविद्योस्मीति राम १३
Final_Translation: Indeed, a certain specific object must necessarily be made the object of concentration. When a part of that taught object is brought into focus, even the most subtle subject, extending all the way up to liberation, is grasped. It is solely for this purpose that this mental purification is prescribed. When the fluctuating mental modifications are absent, and the state of mastery over that object has arisen, he becomes capable of concentrating upon this or that object. And such being the case, faith, energy, mindfulness, and absorption will arise for him without obstruction.   "Or [the state of concentration] accompanied by sorrowless radiant light pertaining to the Purusha."   An emergent activity of the mind maintains a binding stabilization of the mind for one who holds [it] within the lotus of the heart, [namely] of the Knower of the intellect. From the realization of the intellect, which is radiant and sky-like, stability arises there from clarity. Then, that [mind], whose nature is like the brilliance of the sun, moon, planets, and jewels, is perceived in various forms. And when the mind has attained absorption in ego-awareness (asmitā), it becomes tranquil, infinite, resembling a waveless great ocean, consisting of mere ego-awareness. Concerning this, it has been said: "Having distinctly known the atom-sized Self as 'I am,' [he attains peace].'"

Final_Translation: I see You everywhere with infinite forms, possessing countless arms, stomachs, mouths, and eyes. O Lord of the Universe, O Cosmic Form, I see neither Your end, nor Your middle, nor yet Your beginning.

Final_Translation: That which brings about the conjunction of ritual tantras, proper time, space, and remedial medicines; which acts through purification and pacification, employing warming agents and various preparations of herbs. Through the sequential mastery of bodily knowledge and its application, it is the ultimate supreme wisdom. For emesis, honey is administered alongside oils by experts. The devoted physician, eager for scriptural knowledge, and radiant like the sun, speaks auspiciously. This is the unfailing application of mantra. Sanskrit_OCR_Text: पश्यामि देवांस्तव देव देहे सर्वांस्तथा भूतविशेषसंघान् । ब्रह्माणमीशं कमलासनस्थमृषींश्च सर्वानुरगांश्च दिव्यान् ॥ १५ ॥
